Content:
Many people don`t know this, but the McDonald`s app is worldwide. You use the same app in any part of the world. You just can`t use your account across countries. 
 
 When I moved to Singapore, I was pleasantly suprised that by flicking the country switch, my app is now Singaporean (although I do need to sign up again). But when I hop over to JB, I flip the switch again and all my Malaysian McD reward points comes back. Really cool. This opposed to the Starbucks, Pizza Hut or KFC apps, that stops working when I crossed the border into Singapore.
 
 Unfortunately, this means any outage hitting any country knocks it out for everyone.

Content:
Nope. Just some unfortunate events. Maybe too many McDonalds in other countries holding promos at the same time.
 
 I flipped my McD app to Malaysia to see what promos are going on there and they`re having a 10.10 flash sale. 
 
 Edit: seems that McDonald`s has took note of my country crossing. Flipped to Philippines (they`re also holding 10.10 flash sales BTW) and apparently I don`t even need to sign up for another account anymore it just logs me in using my SG account, and on that note my SG account (signed up using same email address as my MY account) has also apparently merged into my MY account. Very cool, wish more global franchises will do this. At this point the Pizza Hut, KFC, Nando`s and Starbucks app on my phone are useless in Singapore, but good to know McD has my back. Apparently Domino`s new app is also supposed to be global but I haven`t tested it thoroughly, the new app downloaded into my phone and decided to only show Singapore restaurants.

Title: Is jb city sq mall rly much cheaper than sg price?
Content: minamikaze said: Things that are worth it in JB: - Massage at holiday plaza, solid and legit, 90 RM for 120 minutes. This is less than 1/3 the price in SG. - Services like facial, hairstyling etc at KSL, all probably half the price or less than that of SG - If you like Starbucks it's probably about 20% cheaper, but somehow their drinks there don't taste as good - Baby clothes are much cheaper - I don't find their hawker food that cheap, it's maybe 10-20% cheaper only. Just mainly to enjoy different taste that's all. More worth it to eat their restaurant food. Guoma near City Square is like S$18, it's not the best hotpot buffet out there but more than enough for my peasant tastes. Title: China & hk stocks/ etfs
Content: stanlawj said: Shaun Rein has this to say: "2 months ago, the smartest people in the room told me China was Uninvestable. One famed billionaire laughed at me when I said it was time to look at Chinese equities again. He said he'd never invest in China again because he said China was becoming Maoist and Xi wanted to return to the Cultural Revolution days (like really, who would ever want that? The current leaders suffered the most during the CR and would do anything to prevent China from returning to those dark days). A group of hedge fund managers looked at me like I had a second head when I said 2024 will be remembered as a Golden Year for investors who took the risk and plunged back into China. Now, 2 months later, HK has the best performing stock market of the major indices, climbing 25% over the year. Fortunes have been made the last few weeks. Crazy fortunes. JD stock doubled. Long-term, it's not smart to bet against America. It's also not smart to bet against China too. I'm not optimistic for Europe and semi optimistic for India - the US and China will remain the key markets for brands. The reality is China is NO longer the no brainer investment destination like it used to be - in the short term, there are a lot more risks internationally (Biden's China containment strategy for one), as well as domestic ones (Xi's Common Prosperity Drive). If you are Intel, you'll never have another shot at the lucrative China market. The Biden Regime's sanctions have ensured that Chinese companies will never trust that they can rely on the US supply chain ever again. Instead they'll buy Chinese tech and tech from countries that China can trust. Whether Trump or Harris wins, China will never again be a major profit driver for American tech companies. But in the medium and long term, it would be a huge mistake to bet against China for many sectors. Why? Despite the weak economy, China will still account for 1/3 of global growth this year. The size of the middle class will swell from 400 million to 800 million in the next 5-10 years. China will be the next China for consumer brands like Zara, Hoka, Adidas. The key is understanding consumer trends, as well as regional ones. Estee Lauder should be booming in China but it's not - their strategy is all wrong. Same with Nike. While consumers in Shanghai are miserable and still have PTSD from the Shanghai Lockdown, consumers in Changsha are bullish and shopping like crazy. Starbucks is dead in Shanghai but still has some room to grow in lower tier cities. Brands and investors need to know what sectors, what regions and segments will do well. If you're stupid, you'll say China is Uninvestable because you buy into the disinformation in Bloomberg and WSJ. If you're smart, you'll keep your eyes & ears to the ground and know when to invest and when not. Less than 2 weeks before my book is launched. Good timing now that investors realize there are still opportunities in China. My book provides a good guidebook on how to invest in China over the next 5 years" Source TLDR: it's not going to be a smooth easy ride. Domestic semicon will do well. Lower tier cities are growing faster than the top tier cities (where the rich are screwed by property losses). Click to expand... did he say anything about the recent plunge though?

may 5 level siguro ng mga mahihirap
 level 1 eto yung walang bahay mga taong pagala gala sa kalsada.
 level 2 eto naman yung mga nakatira sa squatters area may maliit silang bahay walang gamit kungdi upuan at pamesa.
 level 3 nakatira din sa squatters area pero ang kaibahan sa level 2 sila at mas maayos na bahay halos kumpleto ang gamit sa bahay.
 level 4 hindi sila nakatira sa squatters area kumpleto ang mga kagamitan sa kanilang mga tahanan nakakakpag aral ang kanilang mga anak. nakakain ng 4 beses sa isang araw.
 level

there are maybe 5 levels of the poor
 level 1 here are the homeless people wandering the streets.
 level 2 here are those who live in the squatters area, they have small houses with nothing but chairs and tables.
 level 3 also lives in the squatters area but the difference is that they are level 2 and have a better house, the house is almost fully furnished.
 level 4 they don't live in squatters area their homes are fully equipped their children can study. ate 4 times a day.
 level
 here are those who are not poor but pretend to be poor. Those who complain that life is hard now but can eat 5 times a day, some still get midnight snacks.
